title: node_types demand_weight fail-fast rules (integer-only + >= 0) have no negative rows in the fail-fast suite
detail: Round-2 audit bar: 'a rule with no negative row = a gap.' These two node_types rules are the only fail-fast rules in the diff without negative rows; a silent-default regression in either would pass every test.
recommended_fix: Add two node_types rows to test_catalogs_load_failfast: demand_weight 1.5 -> 'must be an integer (no decimals)', demand_weight -1 -> 'must be >= 0' (needs a bad-NT document wiring in check_reject).

title: load_demo_replay regressed: delete(demo.nodes/draws/spawns) removed while adding delete(demo.demolishes) — three dynamic arrays leak per call
evidence:
harness/run.odin:305-309 (current):
	cfg.session.goal = demo.win_goal
	cfg.session.cap_ms = demo.lose_cap_ms
	delete(demo.demolishes) // r1 note: the sibling loaders leaked this too
	delete(demo.captures)
	return cfg
git diff v2 -- harness/run.odin (same hunk, base had three more frees):
-	delete(demo.nodes)
-	delete(demo.draws)
-	delete(demo.spawns)
Callers: harness/drift.odin:44 (load_demo_replay per demo, 9 demos) and harness/run.odin:422 (run_replay); demo_replay_destroy (run.odin:275) frees only cfg.nodes/cfg.spawns, not demo's arrays.
detail: The r1 fix #11 (demolishes free) landed, but the same hunk dropped the three sibling frees — each load_demo_replay call now leaks demo.nodes/draws/spawns backings. The r1 leak family regressed at the exact site it was fixed.
recommended_fix: Restore delete(demo.nodes), delete(demo.draws), delete(demo.spawns) alongside delete(demo.demolishes) in load_demo_replay.

title: catalogs_load never frees the five json.parse trees — the new 46-call fail-fast suite leaks ~800 KiB per `odin test` run (leak report in the gate output)
evidence:
core/catalog.odin — five parses, no delete(v) anywhere in catalogs_load:
211:		v, e := json.parse(src.node_types, parse_integers = true)
251:		v, e := json.parse(src.pipe_tiers, parse_integers = true)
278:		v, e := json.parse(src.packet_types, parse_integers = true)
344:		v, e := json.parse(src.demand, parse_integers = true)
434:		v, e := json.parse(src.balance, parse_integers = true)
odin test core (re-run at abe578b):
[WARN ] --- < 802.84KiB/ 1.03MiB> < 804.71KiB> (  365/ 5393) :: core.test_catalogs_load_failfast
        +++ leak        11B @ 0x6228EAC9F [catalog.odin:251:catalogs_load()]
        +++ leak       896B @ 0x622879280 [catalog.odin:251:catalogs_load()]
        +++ leak        10B @ 0x6228EDFBA [catalog.odin:344:catalogs_load()]
detail: Each check_reject/check_ok call (46 in the suite) leaks 5 parse trees; the new packet_types/demand blocks (278/344) extend the pre-existing pattern and make it loud in the CI gate. No sim behavior, but real + verifiable.
recommended_fix: delete(v) each parsed tree in catalogs_load after extracting fields; catalog id/display strings are parser clones (unquote_string -> clone_string), so re-clone them (strings.clone) so they outlive the tree — then odin test reports zero leaks.

title: Flow-level §3.3 pin exercises only uniform sink weights — the node demand_weight -> weighted_pick wiring is never tested with a non-uniform weight
detail: A wiring bug that ignored the catalog weight (always returning 1) would pass every flow-level test; only unit-level weighted picks pin non-uniformity. The node demand_weight field is this PR's new attractor data — its flow path is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Set one qa_fixture residential demand_weight = 3 and assert the flow-level dst histogram follows the 1:3 (or 1:1:3) ratio ± 3-sigma in test_director_spawns_by_spec.

title: catalogs_hash_sources fold of the new packet_types/demand bytes has no unit pin — a dropped source in the fold would pass every gate silently
evidence:
core/determinism_test.odin:23 (unit tests use a constant, not the fold):
TEST_CATALOG_HASH :: u64(0x0123456789ABCDEF)
core/determinism_test.odin:114 (the only hash pin — the primitive):
test_fnv1a64_conformance :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
core/catalog.odin:502-506 (the fold to pin):
	fold(&h, src.node_types)
	fold(&h, src.pipe_tiers)
	fold(&h, src.packet_types) // 3.1: sim-relevant (drives spawns) — folds into the replay-binding hash
	fold(&h, src.demand)       // 3.1: sim-relevant (the demand director's data)
	fold(&h, src.balance)
No test mutates packet_types/demand bytes and asserts the hash moves; drift's catalog_hash mutation flips a header byte (the binding), not the fold.
detail: The fold is the ODN-11 binding for the new catalogs; if it dropped a source, bless+replay stay internally consistent and every gate (including the era-3 golden) still passes. Regression would be invisible.
recommended_fix: Unit-pin the fold: assert catalogs_hash_sources changes when packet_types or demand bytes differ, and stays stable when only cosmetic (palette) bytes differ.
